value.name: Daniel admits confusion about Lucia's feelings
value.description: Daniel says he has long confused what Lucia would have hated with what he himself would have hated on her behalf.
evidence: I do not think I know what she would have hated. I think I know what I would have hated, on her behalf, and I think I have been confusing the two things for a long time, and I think Lucia has known I was confusing the two things for a long time, and I think Rosa has known it longer than either of us

value.name: Daniel apologizes to Rosa
value.description: Daniel tells Rosa he owes her a larger apology than he can make that morning and promises to try over time.
evidence: I owe you an apology," he said, "that is larger than I can make this morning. I am not going to try to make it this morning. I am going to try to make it over time. I want you to know that I know I owe it.

value.name: Rosa accepts Daniel's apology conditionally
value.description: Rosa responds that she needs the apology to be true rather than large or performative, and Daniel agrees.
evidence: "I do not need the apology to be large. I need it to be true. A small true apology is better than a large performed one. You understand."

value.name: Rosa asks to speak to the counselor
value.description: Rosa addresses Asha as counselor and asks permission to say something.

value.name: Rosa distinguishes the codicil from the letter
value.description: Rosa explains that she has been thinking since Monday about what Daniel's mother wanted and separates the legal codicil from the mother's wish in the letter.
evidence: "I have been thinking, also," Rosa said. "Since Monday. I have been thinking about what your mother" — she looked at Daniel, then at Lucia — "what your mother wanted. The codicil says one third, one third, one third. The letter says she wanted us to be kind. These are two different documents. They do not say the same thing. The codicil is the law. The letter is the wish."

value.name: Rosa begins to assert her long service
value.description: Rosa invokes her thirty-one years as a housekeeper to establish her authority before her thought is cut off in the excerpt.
